pr.title: fix(cli): skip navi upgrade re-download when already on the latest
pr.body: `navi upgrade` re-downloaded and reinstalled the latest release on every run, so re-running kept re-fetching it. `upgrade()` had no installed-vs-latest check and ignored its `--force` param (`_force`). Now it compares the installed version against the latest remote release (the same `remote_release_versions()` source `downgrade`/`maybe_hint_update` use) and no-ops when already current: ``` navi 0.1.9 is already the latest release; nothing to upgrade (use --force to reinstall) ``` `--force` (already documented, now wired up) bypasses the check. The check is best-effort: a network/parse failure falls through and installs as before, so a transient outage can't block an upgrade. Decision logic is a pure `upgrade_needed()` helper with unit tests (current, behind, ahead, forced, unknown-latest). Forward-looking like all self-upgrade fixes: the first upgrade *onto* a build containing this still re-downloads; subsequent runs then no-op. Closes #59. Closes #59 - 🟣 ~~[fix(cli): skip navi upgrade re-download when already on the latest (#60)](https://github.com/lararosekelley/navi/pull/60)~~ (merged) 👈 - `main` --- Stack managed by [git-stk](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk)

expected.description: The already-latest check compares against git tags, which exist before the release is published, so upgrade reinstalls the current version in a loop.
